title: Finding work in Boston through brother Herman and Joe Steele
summary: The first year he worked in restaurants; then his brother Herman's Elks bands spread his name and he began gigging with pianist Joe Steele.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, how did you go about getting yourself work in the Boston area, 'cause nobody knew you -
Well, that's contact, you know. See, for an instance, my brother, he played a little trombone in a amateur Elks' band they called it, see -
Your brother Joe was in the -
Just died a few years, two years -

He could play a little trombone in a Elks' bands, and he had about 2, 3 bands of that type up there, big military bands. Then he would tell people, and they, and the word would get around, see. And I think, I think - I think the first, this is the first band that Joe Steele - I think it was Joe Steele the pianist who graduated from the New England Conservatory. And that was dance also, booked for dancing, you see.
So the first year, the first year you were in Boston most of your -
The first year I in Boston, I didn't have nothin' to do, I worked in restaurants, didn't I tell you?
[ ] that restaurant, you know, I had fallen arches, remember I told you that already.
Right. So the first year in Boston you weren't able to jump right into the musical world -
You didn't know anybody. Then a little bit later on through your brother Herman, you worked sort of semi-amateur, semi-pro connections. You sort of slowly got -
And you went around and - what do you mean, you went around and sat in or went around and applied -
No, didn't send in, I went around and it met people -
